# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `sst docs` from the engine's registries. Edit the registries, not this file. -->

Run `sst <command> --help` in a terminal for a one-screen summary: the
command's first paragraph and each option's first sentence. `sst <command>
--help --full` prints the same text as this page. Every command that reports
results accepts `--output json`, which prints exactly one versioned JSON
envelope on stdout and nothing else.

## Commands

| Command | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`sst init`](#sst-init) | Scaffold SST into an existing dbt project without overwriting a file. |
| [`sst debug`](#sst-debug) | Show the resolved configuration, profile, target, and registry, and test the connection. |
| [`sst migrate`](#sst-migrate) | Rewrite an earlier project into the 1.0 dialect: `split` its lists, then rewrite its `refs`. |
| [`sst migrate refs`](#sst-migrate-refs) | Rewrite references as template calls, move old settings under config:, and label filters. |
| [`sst migrate split`](#sst-migrate-split) | Write each listed member to a file of its own, tool group members to their group's folder. |
| [`sst enrich`](#sst-enrich) | Fill dbt model column metadata from the warehouse, editing the model YAML in place. |
| [`sst format`](#sst-format) | Rewrite YAML into canonical form: indentation, key order, and `\|-` block scalars. |
| [`sst compile`](#sst-compile) | Compile every artifact and write the canonical manifest, offline. |
| [`sst validate`](#sst-validate) | Validate every offline rule, with optional connected checks. |
| [`sst baseline`](#sst-baseline) | Write and maintain the baseline file of known, not yet fixed, diagnostics. |
| [`sst baseline add`](#sst-baseline-add) | Baseline every current instance of CODE, or with --all-warnings every current warning. |
| [`sst baseline prune`](#sst-baseline-prune) | Remove the entries no current diagnostic matches; the only way an entry leaves the file. |
| [`sst baseline renew`](#sst-baseline-renew) | Re-date the baseline --expires-in days from today, recording --reason as its audit record. |
| [`sst baseline show`](#sst-baseline-show) | List the baseline's entries: those of one --code, or with --expired only once it has expired. |
| [`sst list`](#sst-list) | List compiled artifacts and their cached application status, optionally of one TYPE. |
| [`sst lineage`](#sst-lineage) | Show what NODE reads and what reads it: dbt models and sources, members, and artifacts. |
| [`sst plan`](#sst-plan) | Observe live Snowflake state and compute a non-writing plan. |
| [`sst apply`](#sst-apply) | Apply a current reviewed plan; smoke probes never run here. |
| [`sst diff`](#sst-diff) | Compare two states -- local, a dbt target, or a saved plan -- and list what differs. |
| [`sst test`](#sst-test) | Run the smoke and eval suites: those --suite names, else every one that applies. |
| [`sst explain`](#sst-explain) | Explain one diagnostic code from the registry: no project, configuration, or connection. |
| [`sst docs`](#sst-docs) | Write the generated reference pages under docs/reference/. |
| [`sst clean`](#sst-clean) | Remove local SST build artifacts only; never touch Snowflake. |
| [`sst drop`](#sst-drop) | Break-glass: drop exactly one object SST owns from one target, and forget it in state. |
| [`sst state`](#sst-state) | Repair a target's state table: recover entries it lost, convert its kind, or release a lock. |
| [`sst state convert`](#sst-state-convert) | Rebuild the state and lock tables as hybrid or standard tables, keeping the old ones. |
| [`sst state recover`](#sst-state-recover) | Record what state lost, from ownership markers and content digests on the target's live objects. |
| [`sst state unlock`](#sst-state-unlock) | Release the target's run lock held by a run that will never end, live or expired. |
| [`sst agent-kit`](#sst-agent-kit) | Install SST's skills for a coding agent into this project, and keep them current. |
| [`sst agent-kit install`](#sst-agent-kit-install) | Install the kit's skills for each --agent, writing only files that are not there. |
| [`sst agent-kit remove`](#sst-agent-kit-remove) | Remove the kit's skills, or those --only names, from each --agent, else every agent installed. |
| [`sst agent-kit status`](#sst-agent-kit-status) | Show each skill's state against the kit of the SST now installed; change nothing. |
| [`sst agent-kit upgrade`](#sst-agent-kit-upgrade) | Bring every installed skill to the kit of the SST now installed. |
| [`sst ask`](#sst-ask) | Talk to AGENT as it compiles now, publishing nothing; with QUESTION, ask it once. `-` reads stdin. |

## Global options

These go before the command name.

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--version` | flag |  | Show the version and exit. |
| `--output / -o` | table\|plain\|agent\|json\|yaml\|csv |  | `table` (default), `plain` (`table` without colour), `agent` (short fixed-grammar text for coding agents), or `json`, else `$SST_OUTPUT`; `list` also takes `yaml` and `csv`. With neither set, a run whose stdout is not a terminal defaults to `agent` when a coding agent's variable is set (`SST_AGENT`, `CLAUDECODE`, `COCO_AGENT`, `CURSOR_AGENT`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `GEMINI_CLI`; `0` or empty is unset) and says so. A format the command does not take is refused (SST-PRT106). |
| `--verbose / -v` | flag |  | Add each diagnostic's phase and fingerprint, and report each file the run's parse cache served (SST-LOD201). Cannot be combined with `--quiet`. |
| `--quiet / -q` | flag |  | Show error diagnostics only, with no counts line or progress lines; the report still prints. |
| `--log-level` | debug\|info\|warn\|error |  | Threshold for log records on stderr, else `$SST_LOG_LEVEL`, else `warn`. The libraries SST runs, such as the Snowflake connector, log each request at `info`, so `info` shows those. Independent of `--verbose`. |
| `--no-color` | flag |  | No ANSI colour, else `$SST_NO_COLOR`; a non-empty `$NO_COLOR` does the same. Wins over `--color`. |
| `--color` | auto\|always\|never |  | When to colour `table` output: `auto` (the default) on a terminal, `always` even through a pipe, as a CI log viewer renders it, or `never`; else `$SST_COLOR`. Under `auto`, a non-empty `$FORCE_COLOR` or `$CLICOLOR_FORCE` turns colour on and `$NO_COLOR` off. No other format is ever coloured. |
| `--project-dir` | DIRECTORY |  | Project root, else `$SST_PROJECT_DIR`, else the current directory: where `sst_config.yml` and `dbt_project.yml` are. |
| `--config` | PATH |  | Read this configuration file, else `$SST_CONFIG`, instead of discovering one in the project. |
| `--profiles-dir` | DIRECTORY |  | Look for `profiles.yml` here first, else in `$SST_PROFILES_DIR`; then in `$DBT_PROFILES_DIR`, the project root, and `~/.dbt`. The first that has one wins. |
| `--manifest` | FILE |  | Read this dbt `manifest.json` instead of running `dbt parse`. |
| `--allow-unsupported-manifest-schema` | flag |  | Read a dbt manifest of an unsupported schema version, for this run only. |
| `--allow-stale-manifest` | flag |  | Accept a manifest SST did not write (`--manifest`, or `dbt.invoke: false`) that is older than the files it describes, for this run only. |
| `--baseline` | FILE |  | Read this baseline file of known warnings, which must exist, instead of the project's `.sst/baseline.json`, read when it exists. |
| `--no-baseline` | flag |  | Ignore the baseline for this run: every diagnostic is shown and blocks as declared. |
| `--show-baselined` | flag |  | Show baselined diagnostics instead of counting them. |
| `--show-info` | flag |  | Show info diagnostics instead of counting them; a cascade needs `--show-cascade`. |
| `--show-cascade` | flag |  | Show cascade diagnostics, follow-ons downgraded to info, instead of counting them. An override promoting a cascade's code reports it at that severity, as no longer a cascade. |
| `--show-all-occurrences` | flag |  | Show every occurrence of a code, not the first three of four or more. |

## Exit codes

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | `OK` | Success. For `sst plan`, nothing to change: every live object carries the marker state records, and the properties plan compares are as apply read them back. |
| 1 | `ERROR` | Errors were reported, an apply, a test suite, or a check failed, or an apply skipped a blocked change. |
| 2 | `CHANGES` | Declared and actual state differ: `sst plan` found changes, `sst diff` found the two states differ, or `enrich --check`, `format --check`, `docs --check`, `migrate refs`, or `migrate split` found something to rewrite. |
| 3 | `USAGE` | The command line is invalid. |
| 4 | `CONFIG` | The project, its configuration, or a saved plan cannot be used. |
| 5 | `CONNECTION` | Snowflake could not be reached, rejected the credential, refused a privilege, or did not finish in time; the diagnostic code says which, so a retry fixes only some of them. |
| 130 | `INTERRUPTED` | The run was interrupted: Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP, end of input, or a declined prompt. Any command can return it. |

## sst init

Scaffold SST into an existing dbt project without overwriting a file.

Writes `sst_config.yml`, with every policy key at its documented default, and creates the
`semantic_views` directory under the semantic models directory it names. On a terminal
(stdin and stderr both terminals) it asks for that directory, unless --skip-prompts or
--output json; off one it takes the default. A file or directory
that exists is left as it is, and an existing configuration's `project.semantic_models_dir`
is the directory used. With --check-only nothing is written, and the command exits
1 unless the configuration file and the semantic views directory exist. Exit 4 when the
directory is not a dbt project.

```text
sst init [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--skip-prompts` | flag |  | Accept every default without prompting. |
| `--check-only` | flag |  | Report whether the setup is complete; create nothing. |

## sst debug

Show the resolved configuration, profile, target, and registry, and test the connection.

Reports the SST version and, when SST runs dbt for the manifest, the `dbt` on `PATH` it
runs and that dbt's version; every configuration path discovery checked; the registered
artifact types; where the dbt manifest comes from (`--manifest`, the file on disk under
`dbt.invoke: false`, or the `dbt.command` SST runs), its schema, and the schema versions
`dbt.manifest_schema_versions` accepts; which SST installed the project's agent kit, and
whether it is this one; and the resolved target: profile, role, warehouse,
database, schema, state table, and how it authenticates, never a credential. The
connection is then opened, and its role and account reported; with --no-connect nothing
connects. --snowflake-signatures reports instead how often Snowflake refusals went
unrecognised, from `sst_target/run_log.jsonl`, offline.

Exit 0 when everything resolved, 1 when a resolved value is invalid, 4 when the configuration
or profile cannot be, and 5 when the connection fails.

Diagnostics:
    SST-CFG001: there is no configuration file.
    SST-DBT017: the dbt manifest on disk declares a schema the run does not accept.
    SST-DBT027: SST runs dbt for the manifest, and dbt cannot be run; exit 1.
    SST-PRT001: the connection could not be opened.
    Each code the configuration file's own checks report, at exit 1 when one is an error.

```text
sst debug [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--no-connect` | flag |  | Report everything but the connection, offline. |
| `--snowflake-signatures` | flag |  | Report how often Snowflake refusals went unrecognised, from the run log. |

## sst migrate

Rewrite an earlier project into the 1.0 dialect: `split` its lists, then rewrite its `refs`.

The two commands are independent and either may run first; each is a dry run until --write.

Subcommands: [`sst migrate refs`](#sst-migrate-refs), [`sst migrate split`](#sst-migrate-split).

## sst migrate refs

Rewrite references as template calls, move old settings under config:, and label filters.

Reads every YAML file under `project.semantic_models_dir` and `project.tools_dir`, each agent
file and eval file under `project.agents_dir`, each hook manifest under `project.hooks_dir`,
each command under `project.commands_dir`, and the configuration file's `tool()` calls.
Dry-run by default: exit 2 when rewrites are pending, 0 when there are none, and 1 when
something sits where no rewrite is safe, each such place named on stderr. With --write the
files are rewritten, and the command exits 0, or 1 while such a place remains.

```text
sst migrate refs [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--write` | flag |  | Rewrite the files in place; without it, only report. |

## sst migrate split

Write each listed member to a file of its own, tool group members to their group's folder.

Reads every YAML file under `project.semantic_models_dir` and `project.tools_dir`, and the
configuration file, whose `skills.catalog`, `skills.stage` and `skills.extensions` move to
the `skills:` root and the `plugins:`, `profiles:` and `extensions:` blocks. A file that
would overwrite one already there is left whole and named on stderr. Dry-run by default:
exit 2 when a split is pending, 0 when there is none, and 1 when a file is left whole or a
configuration key needs a hand edit. With --write the files are written, then the lists
they came from removed, and the command exits 0, or 1 while such a file remains.

```text
sst migrate split [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--write` | flag |  | Write the new files and remove the old; without it, only report. |

## sst enrich

Fill dbt model column metadata from the warehouse, editing the model YAML in place.

Reads each selected model's relation for its columns and types, and fills what the
model YAML leaves out: column types and data types by default, and with --include sample
values, enums (which bring sample values with them), and synonyms, which Cortex proposes.
Table synonyms go into the model's own `meta.sst`, which every semantic view that uses it
reads. Values already written are kept unless --force names their component. Sample values
and enums read row data, which `enrichment.allow_sample_value_collection: false` refuses.
PATH selects the models whose SQL or YAML file is under it. The relations are the
manifest's, for the resolved target, which must be production-like unless --allow-non-prod
is given.

Exit 0 when done; 1 when a model failed or row data is refused; 2 under --check when files
would change; 3 for a target that is not production-like, a PATH outside the project, or an
unknown component; 4 when no model matches the selection.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT100: the target is not production-like, a PATH is outside the project, or a
        component is unknown; raised.
    SST-CFG038: sample values or enums were asked for, and the project refuses collecting them.
    SST-DIS010: no model matched the selection, one per selector or PATH; raised.

```text
sst enrich [OPTIONS] [PATH]...
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Only these dbt models: `model:<name>` or a bare name; globs such as `fct_*` work, and dbt's graph operators, as in `+model:orders` for the models it is built from. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave these dbt models out; same forms as `--select`. |
| `--include` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Components to fill, repeatable or comma-separated: column-types, data-types, sample-values, enums, column-synonyms, table-synonyms, synonyms, all. Defaults to column-types and data-types. |
| `--force` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Components to derive again over values already written; forcing one includes it. |
| `--database` | TEXT |  | Read every relation from this database instead of the manifest's. |
| `--schema` | TEXT |  | Read every relation from this schema instead of the manifest's. |
| `--allow-non-prod` | flag |  | Enrich from the manifest of a target that is not production-like: one whose name has no `prod`, `production` or `prd` part. Refused without it. |
| `--check` | flag |  | Write nothing; exit 2 when a file would change. |
| `--dry-run` | flag |  | Write nothing; print each file's change as a diff. |
| `--no-detailed-exitcode` | flag |  | With `--check`, exit 0 when files would change, instead of 2. |
| `--fail-fast` | flag |  | Stop at the first model that fails, and write nothing. |

## sst format

Rewrite YAML into canonical form: indentation, key order, and `|-` block scalars.

With no PATH, every artifact type's directory in the configuration and dbt's
`model-paths` are formatted. A PATH is a file, a directory, or a glob, taken from the
project directory when relative; a directory's build, package, and hidden folders are
skipped. --check, --dry-run, --force, and --sanitize compose.

Exit 0 when every file is formatted or already canonical, 1 when a file cannot be read,
parsed, or written, 2 with --check when a file would change, 3 when a PATH names no YAML
file, and 4 with no PATH and no configuration to find the paths in.

Diagnostics:
    SST-CFG001: no PATH was given and there is no configuration file.
    SST-PRT100: a PATH names no YAML file; raised.
    SST-PRT009: a file cannot be read, or is a symbolic link or reached through one; it is
        left as it is.
    SST-PRT008: a file cannot be written; raised.
    SST-LOD001: a file is not YAML; it is left as it is.
    SST-INT003: a file's canonical form would change its value; it is left as it is.

```text
sst format [OPTIONS] [PATH]...
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--check` | flag |  | Write nothing; exit 2 when a file would change. |
| `--dry-run` | flag |  | Write nothing; print each file's change as a diff. |
| `--force` | flag |  | Rewrite every file, even one already in canonical form. |
| `--sanitize` | flag |  | Also remove apostrophes from synonyms and break apart Jinja delimiters in descriptions; sample values are kept as written. |
| `--no-detailed-exitcode` | flag |  | With `--check`, exit 0 when files would change, instead of 2. |

## sst compile

Compile every artifact and write the canonical manifest, offline.

The manifest, `sst_target/manifest.json`, always holds everything that compiled; --select
narrows only what is reported and emitted. --emit-ddl writes each rendered payload, one
file per artifact under a folder named for its type, as `tool/<name>.sql`; and
--emit-agent-spec each agent's specification, one file per agent, and each CoWork
profile's under `cowork_profile/`. With --partial, a compile with errors still writes the
manifest of the artifacts no error touches, and exits 1. Nothing connects: --target,
--defer-target, and --database only decide what names resolve to.

Exit 0 when everything compiled; 1 when an error stopped the compile, the manifest could
not be written, --partial left an artifact out, or two emitted files would collide; 4 when
--select matches nothing.

Diagnostics:
    SST-MAN008: the compile failed, so no manifest was written.
    SST-MAN007: the canonical manifest could not be written.
    SST-PLN033: --partial cannot trace an error to the artifacts it would leave out.
    SST-PRT111: two artifacts of one type would write the same emitted file; nothing is emitted.

```text
sst compile [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--defer-target` | TEXT |  | The `profiles.yml` target whose relations dbt objects resolve to, while publishing to `--target`; else `$SST_DEFER_TARGET`, else `defer.target`. |
| `--no-defer` | flag |  | Defer to no target, whatever `--defer-target`, `$SST_DEFER_TARGET` or `defer.target` say. |
| `--database` | TEXT |  | Resolve refs against this database instead of the target's. |
| `--dbt` | DIRECTORY |  | Read the dbt models from this directory instead of `dbt_project.yml`'s `model-paths`. |
| `--semantic` | DIRECTORY |  | Read the semantic models from this directory instead of `project.semantic_models_dir`. |
| `--emit-ddl` | DIRECTORY |  | Write each artifact's rendered payload into this directory, one folder per type, offline. |
| `--emit-agent-spec` | DIRECTORY |  | Write each agent's rendered specification into this directory, and each CoWork profile's under `cowork_profile/`. |
| `--select` | TEXT |  | Report and emit only these artifacts; the manifest still holds everything. |
| `--partial` | flag |  | Go ahead with every artifact that has no errors and depends on nothing that does; still exits 1 while errors remain. Cannot be combined with `--prune`. |

## sst validate

Validate every offline rule, with optional connected checks.

Exit 0 with no errors, and 1 with errors, or warnings under --strict; a warning the
baseline holds never blocks, and an expired baseline fails the run. The Snowflake syntax
check connects, and runs unless --no-snowflake-syntax-check or
`validation.snowflake_syntax_check: false` turns it off. With --verify-schema, the
columns each semantic view reads are looked up in the warehouse. The syntax check also runs
each model `snowflake.orchestration_models` allows in a throwaway agent. With more than one
thread, the connected checks run on up to that many sessions at once, with the same
findings.

```text
sst validate [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--defer-target` | TEXT |  | The `profiles.yml` target whose relations dbt objects resolve to, while publishing to `--target`; else `$SST_DEFER_TARGET`, else `defer.target`. |
| `--no-defer` | flag |  | Defer to no target, whatever `--defer-target`, `$SST_DEFER_TARGET` or `defer.target` say. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Only these artifacts: a name (`*` and `?` globs), `type:<type>`, `path:<glob>`, `<type>:<name>`, or, where the command takes `--state`, `state:new`, `modified`, `unmodified` or `orphaned`. dbt's graph operators add lineage: `model:orders+` is every artifact `orders` feeds, `+agent:a` all an agent reads, and `2+x` or `x+1` bound the steps; dbt nodes (`model:`, `seed:`, `source:`), members such as `metric:<name>` and `tool_ref:<name>` work inside them. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave these artifacts out; same forms as `--select`. |
| `--database` | TEXT |  | Read from this database instead of the target's; never where an artifact is published. |
| `--strict / --no-strict` | flag |  | Promote every warning to an error, except those marked never promoted; `--no-strict` promotes none. Else `$SST_STRICT`, else `validation.strict`, off when unset. A warning about an artifact the selection leaves out stays one. |
| `--snowflake-syntax-check / --no-snowflake-syntax-check` | flag |  | Connects: compile expressions against Snowflake, and run each model `snowflake.orchestration_models` allows in a throwaway agent. Defaults to `validation.snowflake_syntax_check`, on when unset. |
| `--dbt` | DIRECTORY |  | Read the dbt models from this directory instead of `dbt_project.yml`'s `model-paths`. |
| `--semantic` | DIRECTORY |  | Read the semantic models from this directory instead of `project.semantic_models_dir`. |
| `--verify-schema` | flag |  | Connects: confirm each column a semantic view reads exists in the warehouse. |
| `--threads` | INTEGER RANGE |  | Snowflake sessions to work on at once, 1 to 16, else `$SST_THREADS`, else `generation.threads`, else 4; 1 works serially. Output is the same for any count. |

## sst baseline

Write and maintain the baseline file of known, not yet fixed, diagnostics.

The file is the global --baseline, else `.sst/baseline.json`. Only a code below error that
the registry lets be demoted can be baselined: a baseline suppresses and never demotes.
`add`, `prune`, and `renew` write the file and `show` only reads it. Each runs offline;
`add --target` connects to look for a code only a connection finds, or for every warning,
and `prune --target` to judge an entry only a connection found there. `$SST_TARGET` is
never read.

Subcommands: [`sst baseline add`](#sst-baseline-add), [`sst baseline prune`](#sst-baseline-prune), [`sst baseline renew`](#sst-baseline-renew), [`sst baseline show`](#sst-baseline-show).

## sst baseline add

Baseline every current instance of CODE, or with --all-warnings every current warning.

CODE is a registered code, in any case. The current diagnostics are those an offline
`sst validate` reports, for --target when it is given, narrowed by --select and --exclude.
With --target, a CODE only a connection finds (its precheck is not `local`), or with
--all-warnings every warning, is looked for by the connected `sst validate --target`
instead, and each entry of such a code records the target; an entry of a code an offline
validate finds records none, and a `local` CODE never connects. Additive: an entry is never
removed, and a diagnostic already recorded, or sharing its fingerprint with another current
one, is not added. A new file expires in --expires-in days; an existing one keeps its date,
which only `renew` moves. --all-warnings asks first when there are warnings to add, on a
terminal; off one (stdin and stderr must both be terminals), or with --output json, it needs
--yes.

Exit 0 when the file is written, even with nothing added; 1 when CODE is an error or
non-demotable; 3 when CODE is missing, unregistered, or given with --all-warnings, or a
needed --yes is missing; 5 when --target cannot be reached; 130 when the question is
declined.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT100: no CODE and no --all-warnings, or CODE is not registered; raised. Also, at
        exit 1, CODE cannot be baselined.
    SST-PRT104: CODE and --all-warnings were both given; raised.
    SST-PRT109: --all-warnings without --yes off a terminal, or with --output json; raised.

```text
sst baseline add [OPTIONS] [CODE]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Baseline what `sst validate` finds as this target compiles; a CODE only a connection finds, or every warning, connects, and those entries record the target. Never `$SST_TARGET`; offline without it. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Baseline only the diagnostics of these artifacts. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave the diagnostics of these artifacts out. |
| `--all-warnings` | flag |  | Baseline every current warning; prints the count and needs `--yes`. |
| `--expires-in` | INTEGER RANGE | `180` | Days, 1 to 365, until a new baseline expires; an existing one keeps its date until `renew`. |
| `--note` | TEXT |  | Written into each entry; defaults to `pre-existing at adoption of <code>`. |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Baseline every warning without asking; required off a terminal. |

## sst baseline prune

Remove the entries no current diagnostic matches; the only way an entry leaves the file.

The project is compiled once, for --target when it is given. The offline entries are judged
by an offline validate of that compile, and so is an entry recording --target whose code an
offline validate finds, as an earlier SST recorded one. Any other entry recording --target is
judged by the connected validate, which runs only when there is one; an entry recording
another target is kept. With --select or --exclude, only the entries of the artifacts chosen,
by artifact or source file, are considered. An expired baseline is pruned all the same.

Exit 0 when the file is written, even with nothing pruned; 1 when there is no baseline
file; 5 when --target cannot be reached.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT009: there is no baseline file to prune.

```text
sst baseline prune [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Judge the entries as this target compiles, and the connected ones recorded against it too, connecting only when there is one. Without it, connected entries are kept. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Prune only the entries of these artifacts. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave the entries of these artifacts as they are. |

## sst baseline renew

Re-date the baseline --expires-in days from today, recording --reason as its audit record.

Each renewal is kept in the file, oldest first, with its date, reason, and the expiry it set;
the entries are untouched. Exit 1 when asked for more than 365 days or there is no baseline
file, and 3 when --reason is missing or blank.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT100: --reason is missing or blank; raised. Also, at exit 1, --expires-in is above
        365 days.
    SST-PRT009: there is no baseline file to renew.

```text
sst baseline renew [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--reason` | TEXT |  | Required. Why the baseline is renewed; written into the file. |
| `--expires-in` | INTEGER RANGE | `180` | Days until the renewed baseline expires, at most 365. |

## sst baseline show

List the baseline's entries: those of one --code, or with --expired only once it has expired.

Prints the file's entry count and expiry, then one line per entry shown: its code, artifact,
file, fingerprint, and `offline` or `connected:<target>` for the validate that found it.
With --target, only the entries a validate against it can match are listed: the offline
ones and that target's connected ones. Nothing connects. Without a baseline file it says so
and exits 0.

```text
sst baseline show [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--code` | TEXT |  | Show only the entries of this code. |
| `--expired` | flag |  | Show the entries only once the baseline has expired. |
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Show only the offline entries and those recorded against this target. |

## sst list

List compiled artifacts and their cached application status, optionally of one TYPE.

TYPE is an artifact type such as semantic-views or agents, a member type such as
metrics or verified-queries, or tables. An artifact's status -- pending, applied,
failed, or deactivated -- is what the one local state file under `sst_target` records;
with none there, or more than one target's, every artifact is pending. Without
--no-manifest the manifest `sst compile` wrote is read, and its absence exits 4; with
it, the project's files are compiled in memory, nothing is written, and what fails to
compile is reported and exits 1. A --select or --exclude value that matches nothing is
reported; when the selectors choose no artifact and nothing failed to compile, it exits 4.
--target, --defer-target and --database resolve the in-memory compile as `sst compile`
would, offline; with a compiled manifest, a --target other than the one it was compiled
for is refused (SST-MAN006).

```text
sst list [OPTIONS] [TYPE]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--defer-target` | TEXT |  | The `profiles.yml` target whose relations dbt objects resolve to, while publishing to `--target`; else `$SST_DEFER_TARGET`, else `defer.target`. |
| `--no-defer` | flag |  | Defer to no target, whatever `--defer-target`, `$SST_DEFER_TARGET` or `defer.target` say. |
| `--database` | TEXT |  | Read from this database instead of the target's; never where an artifact is published. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Only these artifacts: a name (`*` and `?` globs), `type:<type>`, `path:<glob>`, `<type>:<name>`, or, where the command takes `--state`, `state:new`, `modified`, `unmodified` or `orphaned`. dbt's graph operators add lineage: `model:orders+` is every artifact `orders` feeds, `+agent:a` all an agent reads, and `2+x` or `x+1` bound the steps; dbt nodes (`model:`, `seed:`, `source:`), members such as `metric:<name>` and `tool_ref:<name>` work inside them. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave these artifacts out; same forms as `--select`. |
| `--long` | flag |  | Also print each artifact's applied fingerprint and published version (a skill's or plugin's alias, the committed version an agent serves, a profile row's VERSION, as the last apply recorded it); `json`, `yaml` and `csv` also carry its source files. |
| `--wide` | flag |  | For a member type, also show the columns each member reads and its expression. |
| `--no-manifest` | flag |  | Compile the project's files in memory instead of reading the compiled manifest. |
| `--dbt` | DIRECTORY |  | With `--no-manifest`, read the dbt models from this directory instead of `dbt_project.yml`'s `model-paths`. |
| `--semantic` | DIRECTORY |  | With `--no-manifest`, read the semantic models from this directory instead of `project.semantic_models_dir`. |

## sst lineage

Show what NODE reads and what reads it: dbt models and sources, members, and artifacts.

NODE is an artifact key such as semantic_view:sales, a member key such as
metric:total_revenue, a dbt node (model:, seed:, snapshot:, test:, exposure:, or
source:&lt;source&gt;.&lt;table&gt;), tool_ref:&lt;name&gt; for a tool another team owns, or a bare name, which
names every node of that name; the name after a kind may glob. Both directions are shown, as
trees, unless --upstream or --downstream picks one, as far as the graph goes unless --depth
stops it; a node where the walk meets someone else's work says so, such as a raw source.
Every reference is drawn, so a node two nodes read is shown under each; --wide adds each
node's Snowflake name and how it uses the node above it, as it does by default for a dimension
or a fact. `-o plain` prints one `<depth> <key>` line per node, upstream depths negative.

Without --no-manifest the manifest `sst compile` wrote is read, and its absence exits 4; with
it, the project is compiled in memory, nothing is written, and what fails to compile is
reported and exits 1. --state marks what changed since that directory's manifest. A NODE
the graph does not hold exits 3 (SST-PRT112).

```text
sst lineage [OPTIONS] NODE
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--upstream` | flag |  | Show only what NODE reads: the dbt models, sources and members it comes from. |
| `--downstream` | flag |  | Show only what reads NODE: the members and artifacts it feeds. |
| `--depth` | INTEGER RANGE |  | Walk at most this many steps from NODE each way; the whole graph by default. |
| `--wide` | flag |  | Also show each node's Snowflake name and how it uses the node above it; on by default when NODE is a dimension or fact. |
| `--state` | DIRECTORY |  | Previous run's build directory, else `$SST_STATE_DIR`: mark each artifact and member that changed since its `manifest.json`. |
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--defer-target` | TEXT |  | The `profiles.yml` target whose relations dbt objects resolve to, while publishing to `--target`; else `$SST_DEFER_TARGET`, else `defer.target`. |
| `--no-defer` | flag |  | Defer to no target, whatever `--defer-target`, `$SST_DEFER_TARGET` or `defer.target` say. |
| `--database` | TEXT |  | Read from this database instead of the target's; never where an artifact is published. |
| `--no-manifest` | flag |  | Compile the project's files in memory instead of reading the compiled manifest. |
| `--dbt` | DIRECTORY |  | With `--no-manifest`, read the dbt models from this directory instead of `dbt_project.yml`'s `model-paths`. |
| `--semantic` | DIRECTORY |  | With `--no-manifest`, read the semantic models from this directory instead of `project.semantic_models_dir`. |

## sst plan

Observe live Snowflake state and compute a non-writing plan.

Exit 0 with nothing to change, 2 with changes pending, and 1 on an error or a blocked change.
Nothing to change means each live object carries the ownership marker state records, and
the properties `plan.drift_check` compares are as apply read them back; an object edited
by hand in either way is blocked (SST-PLN014).
The plan is saved as `sst_target/plan.json` unless --plan-out or --no-plan-out says
otherwise, and each create's and update's statements go to `sst_target/sql`, or --sql-out.
`--names-only` prints only the name of each changed artifact, and wins over `--full`.
Each update is followed by what it changes, member by member, the live object against what
SST renders, cut short where long; all of it is written as a unified diff to
`sst_target/plan.<target>.diff`, or --diff-out, on every plan. `--no-diff` skips reading
the live definitions. What the plan read of the target is recorded as
`sst_target/observation.<target>.json`; `--use-cached-state` plans from the one `--state`
holds instead, without connecting, and reports how old it is.

```text
sst plan [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Only these artifacts: a name (`*` and `?` globs), `type:<type>`, `path:<glob>`, `<type>:<name>`, or, where the command takes `--state`, `state:new`, `modified`, `unmodified` or `orphaned`. dbt's graph operators add lineage: `model:orders+` is every artifact `orders` feeds, `+agent:a` all an agent reads, and `2+x` or `x+1` bound the steps; dbt nodes (`model:`, `seed:`, `source:`), members such as `metric:<name>` and `tool_ref:<name>` work inside them. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave these artifacts out; same forms as `--select`. |
| `--state` | DIRECTORY |  | Previous run's build directory, else `$SST_STATE_DIR`: `state:` selectors compare with its `manifest.json`, and `--use-cached-state` plans from its `observation.<target>.json`. |
| `--defer-target` | TEXT |  | The `profiles.yml` target whose relations dbt objects resolve to, while publishing to `--target`; else `$SST_DEFER_TARGET`, else `defer.target`. |
| `--no-defer` | flag |  | Defer to no target, whatever `--defer-target`, `$SST_DEFER_TARGET` or `defer.target` say. |
| `--prune` | flag |  | Also act on managed artifacts whose source was deleted, as far as each type allows: drop, deactivate, or report. |
| `--partial` | flag |  | Go ahead with every artifact that has no errors and depends on nothing that does; still exits 1 while errors remain. Cannot be combined with `--prune`. |
| `--overwrite` | flag |  | Publish the planned definition over each selected object changed out of band (SST-PLN014) instead of blocking it; an agent keeps its versions and gains one. A saved plan made with it is applied with it. |
| `--plan-out` | FILE |  | Write the saved plan here instead of `sst_target/plan.json`. |
| `--no-plan-out` | flag |  | Do not write a saved plan. |
| `--grants / --no-grants` | flag |  | Read the grants on each object an update replaces, one `SHOW GRANTS` each, to report what a replace would drop (SST-PLN013), and the tags on each semantic view it replaces, to report those the replace removes (SST-PLN039). On by default; `--no-grants` skips the reads. |
| `--use-cached-state` | flag |  | Plan from the observation an earlier `sst plan` recorded in `--state` instead of reading the target, without connecting; the plan says what the target held then, and its age is reported. Requires `--state`; refused with `--snowflake-syntax-check` or `--capture-prior`; composite artifacts are blocked. |
| `--capture-prior` | flag |  | Read the current definition of each live object a planned artifact names, so a review can see what an update replaces and restore it: `GET_DDL` for a semantic view, search service, procedure or function (needs REFERENCES or OWNERSHIP); for an agent, which an update never replaces, the version it serves, its specification, and the `ALTER AGENT` statements that point back at it. A stage, skill, plugin, profile or eval has none. Shown by `--full` and as `prior_definition` in JSON; a read that fails is a warning (SST-PLN037), not a failed plan. |
| `--no-diff` | flag |  | Do not read the live definition each update replaces, so the plan does not show what the update changes member by member: one DESCRIBE, version or staged-file read per update fewer. |
| `--diff-out` | FILE |  | Write what each update changes, member by member, as a unified diff here instead of `sst_target/plan.<target>.diff`. Refused with `--no-diff`. |
| `--sql-out` | DIRECTORY |  | Write each create's and update's statements into this directory instead of `sst_target/sql`. A file an earlier run wrote there, named `<type>__<name>.sql`, `.json` or `.yaml`, for a change this run does not make is removed; any other file is left. |
| `--no-validate` | flag |  | Skip validation: no cycle check, connected check, agent reference lookup, or strict promotion. Only when `sst validate` already ran on the same tree; compile errors still stop the run. Refused with `--snowflake-syntax-check`. |
| `--threads` | INTEGER RANGE |  | Sessions to validate and observe on at once, 1 to 16, else `$SST_THREADS`, else `generation.threads`, else 4; 1 reads serially. The plan is the same for any count. |
| `--full` | flag |  | Also print, under each update, the properties it changes on the object, and the definition it replaces when `--capture-prior` read it; and show each member's diff whole, not cut short. |
| `--names-only` | flag |  | Print the name of each changed artifact, one per line, and nothing else. |
| `--no-detailed-exitcode` | flag |  | Exit 0 when changes are pending, instead of 2. |
| `--strict / --no-strict` | flag |  | Promote every warning to an error, except those marked never promoted; `--no-strict` promotes none. Else `$SST_STRICT`, else `validation.strict`, off when unset. A warning about an artifact the selection leaves out stays one. |
| `--snowflake-syntax-check / --no-snowflake-syntax-check` | flag |  | Connects: compile expressions against Snowflake, and run each model `snowflake.orchestration_models` allows in a throwaway agent. Defaults to `validation.snowflake_syntax_check`, on when unset. |

## sst apply

Apply a current reviewed plan; smoke probes never run here.

Without --plan, apply plans afresh as `sst plan` does, prints the plan, and asks before it
writes; --yes skips the question, and is required with --prune, with --output json, and
whenever stdin or stderr is not a terminal, which apply refuses before it plans. The plan it
asks about shows what each update changes, member by member, as `sst plan` does; with --yes
nothing is shown, so those definitions are not read.
With --plan, the saved plan's selection and --prune are used: --select, --exclude, --prune
and --partial must agree with it, and it must have been made for this target, from the
manifest the project compiles now, observing what Snowflake holds now. The statements are
written to `sst_target/sql`, or --sql-out, before anything runs, and the changes run under
the target's run lock. A failed change skips the changes that depend on it; with
--fail-fast, every change not yet run. `--fail-fast` and `--no-fail-fast` override
`apply.fail_fast`, false by default, for this run. With --partial, the changes no error
touches are applied, those left out are reported, and the run exits 1 while errors remain.
Interrupted by Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP, apply starts no further change, waits for those
running, records what they wrote in state, and releases the lock; a second Ctrl-C stops
the running changes at their next statement.

Exit 0 when every change applied; 1 when a change failed, the plan has errors, or another
run holds the lock; 3 when apply refuses the command line; 4 when the project, its
configuration, or the saved plan cannot be used; 5 when Snowflake cannot be reached; and
130 when the question is declined or the run is interrupted.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT109: --prune or --output json without --yes, or no terminal to ask on; raised.
    SST-PRT107: the run was interrupted while its changes ran.
    SST-PRT104: --partial with --prune, or --no-validate with --snowflake-syntax-check; raised.
    SST-APL005: the saved plan was made for another target.
    SST-MAN030: the saved plan's observation is past its time to live; apply observed afresh.
    SST-APL010: the run took over an expired lock, with --break-stale-lock.
    SST-APL011: another run holds the lock.
    SST-APL013: --temporary would publish to a production-like target.
    SST-APL103: Snowflake ended a session the run used, after it took the lock.

```text
sst apply [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Only these artifacts: a name (`*` and `?` globs), `type:<type>`, `path:<glob>`, `<type>:<name>`, or, where the command takes `--state`, `state:new`, `modified`, `unmodified` or `orphaned`. dbt's graph operators add lineage: `model:orders+` is every artifact `orders` feeds, `+agent:a` all an agent reads, and `2+x` or `x+1` bound the steps; dbt nodes (`model:`, `seed:`, `source:`), members such as `metric:<name>` and `tool_ref:<name>` work inside them. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave these artifacts out; same forms as `--select`. |
| `--state` | DIRECTORY |  | Previous run's build directory, else `$SST_STATE_DIR`, whose `manifest.json` `state:` selectors read. |
| `--defer-target` | TEXT |  | The `profiles.yml` target whose relations dbt objects resolve to, while publishing to `--target`; else `$SST_DEFER_TARGET`, else `defer.target`. |
| `--no-defer` | flag |  | Defer to no target, whatever `--defer-target`, `$SST_DEFER_TARGET` or `defer.target` say. |
| `--plan` | FILE |  | Apply this saved plan. It must still match the compiled project. |
| `--prune` | flag |  | Also act on managed artifacts whose source was deleted, as far as each type allows: drop, deactivate, or report. |
| `--partial` | flag |  | Go ahead with every artifact that has no errors and depends on nothing that does; still exits 1 while errors remain. Cannot be combined with `--prune`. |
| `--overwrite` | flag |  | Publish the planned definition over each selected object changed out of band (SST-PLN014) instead of blocking it; an agent keeps its versions and gains one. A saved plan made with it is applied with it. |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Apply without asking for confirmation. |
| `--fail-fast / --no-fail-fast` | flag |  | Stop at the first failure instead of continuing, and refuse a plan with a blocked change instead of skipping it. Defaults to `apply.fail_fast`. |
| `--threads` | INTEGER RANGE |  | Sessions to plan and apply on at once, 1 to 16, else `$SST_THREADS`, else `generation.threads`. Planning defaults to 4; applying to `skills.+threads`, else 4. |
| `--break-stale-lock` | flag |  | Take over the run lock only once the run holding it has expired (SST-APL010); a live lock is refused all the same (SST-APL011). |
| `--temporary` | flag |  | Publish agents as temporary agents, dropped when the apply's session ends, and skip their evals; views, tools and skills still publish permanently. Refused for a production-like target. |
| `--no-validate` | flag |  | Skip validation: no cycle check, connected check, agent reference lookup, or strict promotion. Only when `sst validate` already ran on the same tree; compile errors still stop the run. Refused with `--snowflake-syntax-check`. |
| `--sql-out` | DIRECTORY |  | Write each create's and update's statements into this directory instead of `sst_target/sql`. A file an earlier run wrote there, named `<type>__<name>.sql`, `.json` or `.yaml`, for a change this run does not make is removed; any other file is left. |
| `--strict / --no-strict` | flag |  | Promote every warning to an error, except those marked never promoted; `--no-strict` promotes none. Else `$SST_STRICT`, else `validation.strict`, off when unset. A warning about an artifact the selection leaves out stays one. |
| `--snowflake-syntax-check / --no-snowflake-syntax-check` | flag |  | Connects: compile expressions against Snowflake, and run each model `snowflake.orchestration_models` allows in a throwaway agent. Defaults to `validation.snowflake_syntax_check`, on when unset. |

## sst diff

Compare two states -- local, a dbt target, or a saved plan -- and list what differs.

A state is `local`, the manifest `sst compile` last wrote; a path ending in `.json`, read
from the project directory, a saved plan, as what it would leave published; or any other
name, a `profiles.yml` target, as what it holds of SST's artifacts now: each one its state
table records whose object still carries SST's ownership marker. --from defaults to
`local` and --to to the resolved target, so `sst diff` alone compares the last compile with
Snowflake, and `--from dev --to prod` compares two targets. An artifact is `new` when only
--to holds it, `orphaned` when only --from does, and `modified` when their fingerprints
differ. Each modified artifact is then compared member by member, as `sst plan` compares an
update: `local` as it compiles for the target it is compared with, a target as its objects
hold it, on up to --threads sessions; --full shows each member's diff whole, and --diff-out
writes them all as a unified diff. Comparing two targets, each one's physical names are first
replaced by what they stand for -- an artifact's object by its key, a dbt model's relation by
`ref('<model>')`, the relation being the deferred target's when `defer.target`, resolved for
that target, names one -- and an artifact whose members then agree is not a difference, so two
targets that publish the same project to different databases agree. A stage tool compares its
comment. A saved plan, an artifact whose definition cannot be read, and every artifact under
--no-diff are compared by fingerprint alone. --select and --exclude keep the differences of
the artifacts they choose.
Diff only reads: it validates nothing, writes no plan, and works on a project that does not
validate; only a target connects.

Exit 0 when they agree, 2 when they differ, 1 when a state cannot be read, 4 when a target
is not declared in `profiles.yml`, and 5 when a target cannot be reached.

Diagnostics:
    SST-MAN001: `local` was asked for and `sst compile` has written no manifest.
    SST-PRT009: a saved plan named by path does not exist, or cannot be read.
    SST-MAN022: a target's state table exists and cannot be read.

```text
sst diff [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--from` | TEXT | `local` | The state compared from: `local` (default), a dbt target, or a saved plan's `.json` path. |
| `--to` | TEXT |  | The state compared with: `local`, a dbt target (default: the resolved one), or a saved plan. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Only these artifacts: a name (`*` and `?` globs), `type:<type>`, `path:<glob>`, `<type>:<name>`, or, where the command takes `--state`, `state:new`, `modified`, `unmodified` or `orphaned`. dbt's graph operators add lineage: `model:orders+` is every artifact `orders` feeds, `+agent:a` all an agent reads, and `2+x` or `x+1` bound the steps; dbt nodes (`model:`, `seed:`, `source:`), members such as `metric:<name>` and `tool_ref:<name>` work inside them. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave these artifacts out; same forms as `--select`. |
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml` that `--to` defaults to, else `$SST_TARGET`, else the profile's. |
| `--full` | flag |  | Also name which recorded fields of a modified artifact differ, and show each member's diff whole, not cut short. |
| `--names-only` | flag |  | Print the name of each differing artifact, one per line, and nothing else. |
| `--no-diff` | flag |  | Compare by fingerprint alone, as an artifact's recorded state says, reading no definition: two targets that publish to different databases then differ in every artifact. |
| `--diff-out` | FILE |  | Write what differs in each modified artifact, member by member, as a unified diff here. Refused with `--no-diff`. |
| `--threads` | INTEGER RANGE |  | Read a target's definitions on up to this many sessions at once, 1 to 16; else `$SST_THREADS`, else `generation.threads`. |
| `--no-detailed-exitcode` | flag |  | Exit 0 when the states differ, instead of 2. |

## sst test

Run the smoke and eval suites: those --suite names, else every one that applies.

Both suites test what `sst apply` published, so they apply once `sst compile` has written
the manifest: the smoke suite when a semantic view compiles, the eval suite when an eval
does. `--select` and `--exclude` narrow every suite to those artifacts. Exit 1 when the
project does not compile, a suite fails, or another run holds the target's run lock; 4
when, with no --suite, no suite applies, or a suite finds the compiled manifest missing
or stale; and 5 when a suite cannot reach Snowflake. Unless one --suite is given, the worst exit wins and
the summary counts the suites that passed, failed, and were skipped: not named, not
applying, or not reached once --fail-fast stopped. The eval suite holds the target's run
lock while it runs, and `--break-stale-lock` takes it over only from a run that has
expired; progress on its runs goes to stderr, except under --quiet or --output json.
`--capture-baseline` exits 3 unless the eval suite runs.

`--unpublished` runs the eval suite, alone unless --suite names smoke too, against each
agent as it compiles now, through temporary agents: it needs no `sst compile` or `sst
apply` first, takes no lock, and reads and writes no baseline or eval state. Only
`tool_selection_accuracy`, which it scores exactly, can fail it; the metrics it judges are
approximate and reported only. It exits 3 with `--capture-baseline`, or with a --suite
that does not name evals.

`--compare-models` runs the eval suite, alone unless --suite names smoke too, as a model
comparison (`cli.compare`): it gates nothing and exits 1 only when a precheck refuses or a
version could not be committed or restored. `--refresh-cost` rereads an earlier
comparison's cost and runs nothing, exiting 4 for a file SST did not write. Both exit 3
with `--capture-baseline`, `--unpublished`, or a --suite that does not name evals.

```text
sst test [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--suite` | smoke\|evals, repeatable |  | Repeatable. `smoke` probes deployed semantic views; `evals` runs agent evaluations. Defaults to every suite that applies. |
| `--select` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Only these artifacts: a name (`*` and `?` globs), `type:<type>`, `path:<glob>`, `<type>:<name>`, or, where the command takes `--state`, `state:new`, `modified`, `unmodified` or `orphaned`. dbt's graph operators add lineage: `model:orders+` is every artifact `orders` feeds, `+agent:a` all an agent reads, and `2+x` or `x+1` bound the steps; dbt nodes (`model:`, `seed:`, `source:`), members such as `metric:<name>` and `tool_ref:<name>` work inside them. |
| `--exclude` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Leave these artifacts out; same forms as `--select`. |
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--defer-target` | TEXT |  | The `profiles.yml` target whose relations dbt objects resolve to, while publishing to `--target`; else `$SST_DEFER_TARGET`, else `defer.target`. |
| `--no-defer` | flag |  | Defer to no target, whatever `--defer-target`, `$SST_DEFER_TARGET` or `defer.target` say. |
| `--threads` | INTEGER RANGE |  | Smoke probes, and eval runs neither `evals.+concurrency` nor an eval's `concurrency` setting paces, run at once, 1 to 16, else `$SST_THREADS`, else `generation.threads`, else 1. |
| `--fail-fast` | flag |  | Stop the smoke or eval suite at its first failing probe or eval, running them one at a time, and run no suite after one that fails. |
| `--capture-baseline` | flag |  | Record this eval run as each eval's new baseline instead of gating it on the stored one. Requires `--reason`, and a run of the eval suite: refused with a `--suite` that does not name `evals`, or no `--suite` when the eval suite does not apply. |
| `--reason` | TEXT |  | Why the baseline is changing; stored with it. Requires `--capture-baseline`. |
| `--unpublished` | flag |  | Run the eval suite against each agent as it compiles now, through temporary agents, publishing nothing: no `sst apply` first, no lock, no baseline, no eval state. `tool_selection_accuracy` is scored exactly and gates on its threshold; `answer_correctness` and custom metrics are judged approximately and never gate. Refused with `--capture-baseline`, or a `--suite` that does not name `evals`. |
| `--compare-models` | TEXT |  | Compare orchestration models on the selected evals' published agents and CoWork profiles: each model in LIST, comma-separated, else each eval's `evals.+candidate_models`, runs on a version committed for it, aliased `EVAL_<MODEL>`, beside the pinned model on the release; the default, the release's alias and the live version end as they were. Runs the eval suite, gates nothing, and writes `compare.json` and `report.html`. Refused with `--capture-baseline`, `--unpublished`, or a `--suite` that does not name `evals`. |
| `--compare-runs` | INTEGER RANGE |  | Runs of each model a comparison makes, at least 1; else each eval's `evals.+compare_runs`, else 2. Requires `--compare-models`. |
| `--compare-report` | DIRECTORY |  | Directory a comparison writes `compare.json` and `report.html` to; else `sst_target/compare/<eval>_<UTC time>/`. Requires `--compare-models`. |
| `--refresh-cost` | FILE |  | Read the usage of the runs a comparison's `compare.json` names again, fill in the cost that was pending, rank and decide again, and rewrite the report where it is. Runs nothing; refused with `--compare-models`. |
| `--break-stale-lock` | flag |  | Take over the run lock only once the run holding it has expired (SST-APL010); a live lock is refused all the same (SST-APL011). |

## sst explain

Explain one diagnostic code from the registry: no project, configuration, or connection.

CODE is a registered 1.0 code, an SST 0.3 code that survives as an alias, or a retired 1.0
number, in any case. A code is shown with its severity, phase, when it is raised, its
message and suggestion, its note, the package modules that name it, the 0.3 codes it came
from, and its docs link; an alias with what it became; a retired number with what
superseded it. --aliases also lists each 0.3 code that resolves to the code; the JSON
envelope always carries them.

Exit 0 when the code is explained, and 3 when it is not a registered code, a 0.3 alias, or
a retired number.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT100: the code is unknown; raised.

```text
sst explain [OPTIONS] CODE
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--aliases` | flag |  | Also list the SST 0.3 codes that resolve to the code, and what each became. |

## sst docs

Write the generated reference pages under docs/reference/.

The error-code, coverage, artifact, command-line, and configuration references are
rendered from the engine's own registries, so they cannot drift from what the engine
accepts; --only picks some of them, and --output-dir writes or checks them elsewhere. Only
a page that differs from the file on disk is written. The coverage page also reads each
code's tests from `tests/codes/` under the project directory. With --check, nothing is
written and the command exits 2 when a page differs or is missing; --no-detailed-exitcode
turns that 2 into 0. Exit 1 when the generator itself fails.

```text
sst docs [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--check` | flag |  | Write nothing; exit 2 when a committed reference page is out of date. |
| `--only` | errors\|coverage\|artifacts\|cli\|config, repeatable |  | Repeatable. Generate only these references: `errors`, `coverage` (the code-to-test matrix), `artifacts`, `cli`, `config`. Defaults to all of them. |
| `--output-dir` | DIRECTORY |  | Write the pages here instead of `docs/reference`. |
| `--no-detailed-exitcode` | flag |  | Exit 0 instead of 2 when there are differences. |

## sst clean

Remove local SST build artifacts only; never touch Snowflake.

Removes `sst_target/` under the project, where SST writes the compiled manifest, saved plans
and observations, statement files, local state, the run log, and `sst ask` transcripts; and
`target/sst/`, where SST wrote them before they moved, when an earlier run left it. Authored files, `.sst/` with its
baseline, and dbt's `target/` are kept. With --dry-run, nothing is removed. Exit 1 when a
build directory cannot be removed, or a symbolic link is on the way to it.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT010: a build directory could not be removed, or is reached through a link.

```text
sst clean [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | flag |  | List what would be removed; remove nothing. |

## sst drop

Break-glass: drop exactly one object SST owns from one target, and forget it in state.

For when `apply --prune` cannot serve, such as a project that does not compile: drop reads
no project artifact and needs no configuration file. The object is one three-part name,
never a pattern; --type picks the DROP statement; --target has no default and
`$SST_TARGET` is not read; the profile is --profile, else `dbt_project.yml`'s `profile:`.
--yes is required on every invocation, and there is no prompt. Only an object carrying
SST's ownership marker is dropped; a skill's or plugin's extension, which carries none, only
when state records it at a version it still lists, and one already gone is forgotten.
Drop holds the target's run lock, as apply does, and
deletes the object's entries from the state table the configuration's `state:` block
names, or, when there is no configuration that reads, the target's default `SST_STATE`.
One audit line goes to stderr before the statement and one after; --quiet does not silence
them, --log-level error does.

Exit 0 when the object was dropped; 1 when Snowflake refused, the object does not exist,
it carries no SST ownership marker, or another run holds or took the lock; 3 when drop
refuses the command line; 4 when the profile or target cannot be resolved; and 5 when
Snowflake cannot be reached.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT100: not exactly one object, a missing or unregistered --type, or no --target;
        raised.
    SST-PRT110: the object is a pattern rather than one name; raised.
    SST-PRT108: the object is not a three-part name; raised.
    SST-PRT109: --yes was not given; raised.
    SST-PRT005: the object does not exist; an extension state records is forgotten.
    SST-PLN024: the object carries no SST ownership marker, or, for an extension, state
        does not record it at a version it still lists.
    SST-APL001: Snowflake refused the DROP.
    SST-APL011: another run holds the lock, or took it before state was updated.
    SST-APL010: an expired lock was taken over, with --break-stale-lock.
    SST-PLN017: an agent apply published names the object; it is dropped all the same.

```text
sst drop [OPTIONS] <DB>.<SCHEMA>.<NAME>
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--type` | TEXT |  | Required. The registered type of the object, which picks the DROP: agent, plugin, semantic_view, or skill. |
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Required. Target from `profiles.yml`; there is no default, and `$SST_TARGET` is not read. |
| `--profile` | TEXT |  | Profile in `profiles.yml`; else `dbt_project.yml`'s `profile:`. Needed outside a project. |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Required on every invocation: it is the confirmation, and there is no prompt. |
| `--break-stale-lock` | flag |  | Take over the run lock only once the run holding it has expired (SST-APL010); a live lock is refused all the same (SST-APL011). |

## sst state

Repair a target's state table: recover entries it lost, convert its kind, or release a lock.

State records what apply published to each target, in the state table `state:` names. These
commands write that table and its lock table, and never a published object.

Subcommands: [`sst state convert`](#sst-state-convert), [`sst state recover`](#sst-state-recover), [`sst state unlock`](#sst-state-unlock).

## sst state convert

Rebuild the state and lock tables as hybrid or standard tables, keeping the old ones.

The state table is copied into a new table of the kind --to names, then the old one is
renamed to `<name>_<KIND>_BAK` and the new one into its place; the lock table is renamed
to its backup the same way and created again, empty. Refused, with nothing changed, while
any target's lock is live, or when the state table's rows change during the copy: run it
while no apply does. Set `state.+table_kind` to the new kind afterwards, or every run
refuses the converted tables (SST-APL031). Hybrid tables cannot sit in a transient
database or schema (SST-APL030), nor on an account that cannot create them (SST-APL035).

Exit 0 when the tables were converted; 1 when the conversion was refused or failed; 3 when
it would have to ask and there is no terminal, without --yes.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT109: there is no terminal to ask on, and --yes was not given; raised.
    SST-APL034: the conversion was refused; nothing was changed.
    SST-APL030: a hybrid table cannot be created in the transient database or schema.
    SST-APL035: the account cannot create hybrid tables.

```text
sst state convert [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--to` | standard\|hybrid, required |  | Required. The kind of table to rebuild the state and lock tables as. |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Convert without asking for confirmation; required off a terminal. |

## sst state recover

Record what state lost, from ownership markers and content digests on the target's live objects.

Plans the target, then records, under the run lock and without writing any object, each
artifact state does not record whose live objects prove they hold the compiled definition,
so `sst plan` then shows it unchanged. A semantic view, tool or agent proves it by the
marker in its comment; a skill or plugin by its aliased version's files and the bundle
prefix they came from, read back byte for byte; a profile by its registry row as Desktop
reads it; an eval by its dataset version's provenance and its staged config's bytes.
Every other unrecorded artifact is listed with what the next apply will do: one SST cannot
prove stays unmanaged (SST-PLN024), and one that holds another definition is published
again. Eval baselines are not recovered.

Exit 0 when recover ran, whatever it recorded; 1 when another run holds the lock or the
plan is refused; 3 when it would have to ask and there is no terminal, without --yes.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT109: there is no terminal to ask on, and --yes was not given; raised.
    SST-APL032: what recover recorded, as a summary.
    SST-APL033: an unrecorded artifact recover could not record, and what apply will do.
    SST-APL011: another run holds the lock.
    SST-APL010: an expired lock was taken over, with --break-stale-lock.

```text
sst state recover [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Record without asking for confirmation; required off a terminal. |
| `--break-stale-lock` | flag |  | Take over the run lock only once the run holding it has expired (SST-APL010); a live lock is refused all the same (SST-APL011). |

## sst state unlock

Release the target's run lock held by a run that will never end, live or expired.

Releases the lock row only while the named run holds it, in one lock transaction, so a lock
another run took meanwhile is kept; the local lock file is released too when it names the
run. A run on this machine whose process is gone needs none of this: the next apply
releases its locks itself (SST-APL010). There is no prompt: --yes is the confirmation.

Exit 0 when the lock was released; 1 when the run does not hold it; 3 without --yes.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT109: --yes was not given; raised.
    SST-APL040: the run's lock was released.
    SST-APL041: the run does not hold the lock, so nothing in Snowflake was released.

```text
sst state unlock [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`; defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--run` | TEXT, required |  | Required. The run id whose lock to release, as SST-APL011 names the holder. |
| `--yes / -y` | flag |  | Required on every invocation: it is the confirmation, and there is no prompt. |

## sst agent-kit

Install SST's skills for a coding agent into this project, and keep them current.

The kit ships inside the package, so each SST installs the skills written for it. Skills go
to `.cortex/skills` (--agent cortex) or `.claude/skills` (--agent claude), and
`.sst/agent-kit.json` records what SST wrote, so `upgrade` and `remove` touch only those
files and never one you changed, unless --force. Nothing connects to Snowflake and nothing
is committed: the files are ordinary changes in the working tree. The kit is for a coding
agent; it is never published, and it may not sit inside a directory SST publishes from.

Subcommands: [`sst agent-kit install`](#sst-agent-kit-install), [`sst agent-kit remove`](#sst-agent-kit-remove), [`sst agent-kit status`](#sst-agent-kit-status), [`sst agent-kit upgrade`](#sst-agent-kit-upgrade).

## sst agent-kit install

Install the kit's skills for each --agent, writing only files that are not there.

Without --agent, the agent whose folder (`.cortex` or `.claude`) the project has; with both
or neither, --agent is required. --only installs just the skills it names, and adds them to
those installed before. A skill already installed is left as it is, even when out of date:
`upgrade` updates it. A folder already holding the kit's files exactly is adopted; any
other folder or file in the way refuses the whole run, and nothing is written.

Exit 0 when the kit is installed, or with --dry-run would be; 1 when something is in the
way or cannot be written; 3 when --only names no kit skill or the agent is ambiguous; 4
when the kit's folder overlaps a directory SST publishes from.

Diagnostics:
    SST-CFG052: the agent's skills folder overlaps a `project.*_dir` directory.
    SST-PRT013: a skill folder or file is in the way.
    SST-PRT100: --only names no kit skill, or no agent can be chosen; raised.

```text
sst agent-kit install [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--agent` | cortex\|claude, repeatable |  | Repeatable. Install for this coding agent: `cortex` (`.cortex/skills`) or `claude` (`.claude/skills`). Defaults to the one whose folder the project has. |
| `--only` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Repeatable. Install only this kit skill; adds to those already installed. |
| `--dry-run` | flag |  | List what would be written; write nothing. |

## sst agent-kit remove

Remove the kit's skills, or those --only names, from each --agent, else every agent installed.

A file SST wrote and nobody changed is removed, with any folder that leaves empty; one you
changed is kept, and stays recorded, unless --force (SST-PRT014). A file SST did not write
is never removed. The lock is removed with the last skill it records. After a partial
removal `upgrade` maintains only the skills still installed; `install` adds others back.

Exit 0 when the skills are removed, kept files included, or with --dry-run would be; 1 when
a file cannot be removed.

Diagnostics:
    SST-PRT014: a file you changed is kept.

```text
sst agent-kit remove [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--agent` | cortex\|claude, repeatable |  | Repeatable. Remove only this agent's skills; defaults to every agent installed. |
| `--only` | TEXT, repeatable |  | Repeatable. Remove only this installed skill. |
| `--force` | flag |  | Also remove files you changed since SST wrote them. |
| `--dry-run` | flag |  | List what would be removed; remove nothing. |

## sst agent-kit status

Show each skill's state against the kit of the SST now installed; change nothing.

Lists, for each --agent, else each agent the lock records, else each agent whose folder the
project has, else both: every kit skill, and any installed one the kit dropped, as
`current`, `outdated` (an upgrade would change it), `modified` (you changed a file SST
wrote), `missing` (its folder is gone), or `not installed`. With --check, exit 2 when any
skill is outdated or missing, as `sst format --check` does for YAML.

```text
sst agent-kit status [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--agent` | cortex\|claude, repeatable |  | Repeatable. Show only this agent; defaults to every agent installed. |
| `--check` | flag |  | Exit 2 when a skill is outdated or missing. |

## sst agent-kit upgrade

Bring every installed skill to the kit of the SST now installed.

Acts for each --agent, else for every agent the lock records. A file SST wrote and nobody
changed is replaced, added, or removed to match the kit; one you changed or deleted is kept
as it is (SST-PRT014 when the kit changed it too) unless --force, which makes every file
match the kit. A skill the kit adds is installed for an agent that installed the whole kit,
and a skill it drops is removed. A file in the way that SST did not write refuses the whole
run, even with --force.

Exit 0 when every installed skill is upgraded, kept files included, or with --dry-run would
be; 1 when something is in the way or cannot be written; 4 when the kit's folder overlaps a
directory SST publishes from.

Diagnostics:
    SST-CFG052: the agent's skills folder overlaps a `project.*_dir` directory.
    SST-PRT013: a file or folder the kit now ships is in the way.
    SST-PRT014: a file you changed is kept although the kit changed or dropped it.

```text
sst agent-kit upgrade [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--agent` | cortex\|claude, repeatable |  | Repeatable. Upgrade only this agent's skills; defaults to every agent installed. |
| `--force` | flag |  | Make every installed file match the kit, overwriting your changes. |
| `--dry-run` | flag |  | List what would change; write nothing. |

## sst ask

Talk to AGENT as it compiles now, publishing nothing; with QUESTION, ask it once. `-` reads stdin.

Connects: each view, search service, tool, skill and sub-agent the agent reaches that
compiles differently from what the target's state records is copied into the agent's
schema, or `agents.+scratch_schema`, as `<NAME>__SST_ASK_<id>`, and the agent's
specification, pointed at the copies, runs over the Cortex Agents REST API, streamed, on a
thread. The copies are dropped and the thread deleted when the session ends; a later
session removes what one that died left, and `--cleanup` removes it now. `--published`
copies nothing and warns of each edit the agent does not see (SST-ASK001). Takes no lock and
writes no state.

Without QUESTION, on a terminal, a conversation opens, with a picker when AGENT is not
named; without a terminal, QUESTION is required. `--transcript` keeps each run's
transcript in `sst_target/ask/`, which `sst clean` removes.

Exit 0 when the agent answered; 1 when the project does not compile, a copy is refused
(SST-ASK008), a tool is unreachable (SST-ASK010) or the run fails (SST-ASK002); 3 for an
empty question, or none without a terminal, or a `--theme` or `$SST_ASK_THEME` that names no
theme; 4 when no agent of that name compiles (SST-ASK003) or `ask.theme` names no theme
(SST-ASK011); and 5 when Snowflake is unreachable or refuses the session.

```text
sst ask [OPTIONS] [AGENT] [QUESTION]
```

| Option | Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--target / -t` | TEXT |  | Target from `profiles.yml`, else `$SST_TARGET`: the agent's names resolve, and its temporary agent runs, there. Defaults to the profile's own default target. |
| `--defer-target` | TEXT |  | The `profiles.yml` target whose relations dbt objects resolve to, while publishing to `--target`; else `$SST_DEFER_TARGET`, else `defer.target`. |
| `--no-defer` | flag |  | Defer to no target, whatever `--defer-target`, `$SST_DEFER_TARGET` or `defer.target` say. |
| `--published` | flag |  | Copy nothing: run the agent on the published views, tools, skills and agents it names, and warn of each edit it does not see (SST-ASK001). |
| `--cleanup` | flag |  | Remove every scratch copy and `sst_ask` thread earlier sessions left, in each agent's scratch schema, then exit. |
| `--show-tools` | flag |  | With QUESTION, also print each tool call the agent made and each tool result, on stderr. |
| `--timeout` | INTEGER RANGE | `600` | Seconds one turn may take before it is cancelled, 1 to 900; default 600. |
| `--transcript / --no-transcript` | flag |  | Keep a transcript in `sst_target/ask/`: each turn whole, rows included, and each specification the agent ran on, replaced after every turn; `--no-transcript` keeps none. Else `ask.transcripts`, else none. `sst clean` removes them. |
| `--theme` | TEXT |  | The conversation's color theme, else `$SST_ASK_THEME`, else `ask.theme`, else `sst-dark`; Textual's own themes are named too, and Ctrl-P changes it for the session. |
